title: Keying Out Charisma
content: Across all the papers I've published in journals over the years, I've cited a Supreme Court decision in only one; the court case was Jacobellis v. Ohio, 378 U.S. 184 (1964), and the citation appears in a paper titled “‘Coevolution’ Between Parsnip Webworms and Wild Parsnips: Should the ‘Co’ Go?” (Berenbaum 1991). The paper was a product of a symposium I attended in Budapest, Hungary, in 1989; its goal was to address a controversy in the literature revolving around the idea that insect herbivory is not a selective force to bring about evolutionary responses in the plants on which they feed. (Yes, that was a major point of contention at one point in time in insect ecology.)
